creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 10, item 2. Alex, 2026-10-25: this looks like an issue, not just a doc gap; decide it.

Inside a fn, `out += [x]` on a list parameter rebinds the local name, so the caller's list is unchanged. `m[k] = v` on a map parameter mutates the caller's map. A recursive flattener that accumulated into a list parameter silently returned nothing:

```rad
fn add_list(out):
    out += ["x"]
fn add_map(m):
    m["k"] = "v"
l = []
add_list(l)   // l is still [ ]
d = {}
add_map(d)    // d is { "k": "v" }
```

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1). Python mutates the caller's list here (list += extends in place). In Rad the parameter name ends up bound to a new list, which the caller never sees.

Options: make `+=` on a list extend in place (breaking for any script that relies on the copy), keep it and have rad check warn when a parameter is rebound by `+=`, or keep it and only document it (the skill-doc card a_2o8vX4jpu already proposes the gotcha). Related: a_2o8vaDjYI, where `+=` inside a fn writes the global while `x = x + v` makes a local.
title: Decide whether += on a list parameter should change the caller's list
